The *Aṅkurapetavatthu* (Pv 21), rendered in English as *The Merchant Aṅkura*, is a narrative text belonging to the *Petavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. Its core theme centers on the principle that acts of giving (*dāna*) unfailingly yield positive karmic fruit [SuttaCentral]. The narrative traditions regarding Aṅkura are prominently connected to multiple canonical suttas and stories throughout the Pali canon, being cited or referenced in the *Chaḷaṅgadānasutta* (AN 6.37), the *Sādhusutta* (SN 1.33), and numerous Jātaka tales, including the *Ādittajātaka* (Ja 424), *Akittijātaka* (Ja 480), *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493), and the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547) [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analyses by DharmaNexus reveal widespread transmission of its verses across the Pali commentary literature, recording 160 matching passages across 14 works [DharmaNexus]. Beyond its primary exposition in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, substantial textual parallels occur in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In particular, segments §42.4–44.1 share direct canonical verse reuse with the *Akittijātaka* (Ja 480) [DharmaNexus], which is also noted as related by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects computational parallels with several Tibetan canonical and paracanonical works, including Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094), the *Mahāvyutpatti* (D4346), the *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2), and Kṣemendra's *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) [DharmaNexus].
